facts.text: The Mist Hunters' forest law, the wood's leave, Rob Ria's bow and his quarrel with Camelot are Living Server writing.

story:
Rob Ria leads the Mist Hunters, the hunters of the old forest who keep their camps in the east of Sauvage, and he will tell anyone who lives long enough to ask that his people hunted there before there was a Camelot to forbid it. They take what the wood allows and nothing else: a deer in its season, a boar that has gone wrong, never a tree, never anything that walks near the knight in green. They call it the wood's leave, and they say the forest knows who has it.

Camelot calls them poachers and outlaws, and Lord Mathius's riders have orders to treat them as such, so the Mist Hunters treat Albion's travellers as Albion treats them. Those who have earned the hunters' trust find Rob Ria a fair man to deal with. He wants a scout's bow of the old pattern, strung with what comes off a gytrash of the Pennines in the dead hours and fletched with what an Arawnite shamaness carries outside the Snowdonia fortress, and he pays for the makings. The woodsmen of Castle Sauvage say he means it for the day the enemy comes down through the northern passes in earnest; the castle's lieutenants say he means it for them. Rob Ria says only that a bow is for whatever needs shooting.

He is quick and close with a blade, and his hunters come to his whistle.
legend: Rob Ria, level 40, east Forest Sauvage with the Mist Hunters (forest hunters, 21-24). Aggressive unless your Mist Hunter standing is good; with good standing he gives The Forest Plot (gytrash in the Pennines at night, Arawnite shamaness outside Snowdonia Fortress, for a bow). If you fight him, clear the hunters around him first: they are the same faction and come with him. A group of 40s handles it.
